frequency_question: How often do executive principals with strong intent and direct authority finalize major contested regulatory measures within a single year?
membership_rule: Includes major finalized rules driven by executive priority with high financial or operational impact. Excludes legislative statutes, judicial injunctions that permanently halt the process, or routine administrative maintenance rules.

cases.name: State Department Public Charge Visa Ineligibility Rule
DHS Asylum Transit Ban Interim Final Rule
HHS Reproductive Health Services Grant Regulation
EPA Mercury and Air Toxics Standards Reconsideration
DOL Independent Contractor Status Final Rule

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named prominent instances; representative of executive-driven priority rulemakings pushed to finalization under high intent.
known_gaps: Does not exhaustively list every minor agency adjustment, focusing instead on high-salience administrative priorities.
skeleton: Executive priority regulatory actions pursued aggressively by politically appointed agency leadership divided by total targeted priority actions initiated within the timeframe.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 identified high-priority executive rulemakings tracked under similar conditions of strong political will and direct administrative capability.
validity_reason: The base rate reflects executive branch administrative follow-through capability, which remains stable across a standard presidential term.
